title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
summary: Active-learned DFT-trained interatomic potentials enabled molecular-dynamics mapping of ammonia–hydrogen phase equilibria. Simulated critical curves rose from about 500 K at 0.1 GPa to roughly 2,000 K near 30 GPa before flattening; planetary implications were conditional on binary-mixture simulations and published interior profiles, with high-temperature curves partly constrained.
ai_technology: Active-learned DFT-trained machine-learning interatomic potentials supplied energies/forces for large-scale molecular dynamics that mapped ammonia–hydrogen phase equilibria.
organization: University of Cambridge; University of Oxford

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Primary v1 reports coexistence simulations using learned interatomic potentials and comparisons with density-functional-theory reference data.
evidence.unknown: Predictions concern the binary ammonia–hydrogen system; planetary implications depend on interior models and some high-temperature behavior is only partly constrained.
